title: BWF unveil hosts for major tournaments as Canada nets World Championships
article_text:
The Badminton World Federation (BWF) governing body has announced hosts for several major tournaments through 2030, with the sport’s flagship events to be spread across North America, Asia, and Europe.

The appointments come as the BWF looks to grow badminton’s global reach by staging its premier tournament in key and emerging markets.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The 2027 edition of the BWF’s showpiece biennial competition, the World Championships, will be staged in Mississauga, Canada, from July 14 to 25, marking the second time the country has hosted the event, after Calgary in 1985.

The showpiece competition will headline a three-tournament swing in North America, featuring the Canada Open and US Open, as the sport looks to boost visibility ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul said: “North America is an important growth market for badminton and the 2027 swing represents a major opportunity to build momentum towards LA28 and showcase our sport to new audiences.

“I congratulate Badminton Canada on securing the BWF World Championships 2027. Mississauga will provide an excellent stage for our flagship individual championship and help further strengthen badminton’s presence across the region.”

Meanwhile, the 2028 edition of the BWF Thomas and Uber Cup Finals, the men’s and women’s national teams’ competition, respectively, will be held in New Delhi, India, while the 2030 edition will be staged in Paris, France.

New Delhi last hosted the event in 2014 and comes after India hosts the 2026 BWF World Championships in the capital.

The mixed team Sudirman Cup Finals 2029 will be staged in Korea, with a host city to be announced in due time. The host for the 2027 edition was announced as Beijing, China, last month.

Leeswadtrakul added: “The hosts selected for our Major Championships represent some of the most important and strategic markets in our sport and share our ambition to deliver exceptional events that inspire athletes, engage fans and strengthen badminton’s global profile.

“We look forward to working closely with each host as we continue to elevate our Major Championships and bring badminton’s biggest moments to more people around the world.”

The BWF has ramped up its efforts to increase the visibility of the sport as it looks towards the next Olympic Games. Late last year, the governing body extended its agreement with sports marketing agency Infront to distribute all media and sponsorship rights on its behalf through 2034.

Infront’s remit covers BWF World Tour events, the World Tour Finals, the BWF World Championships, the Sudirman Cup Finals, and the Thomas & Uber Cup Finals.

title: Ohio State Sidesteps Big Ten-Strauss Sponsorship Amid Sex Abuse Scandal
article_text:
Ohio State University says it has opted out of the football-related promotional components of the Big Ten’s newly announced promotional partnership with German-based workwear maker Engelbert Strauss.

“The Ohio State University appreciates the Big Ten Conference’s work in developing innovative partnership opportunities that benefit the conference and its member institutions,” a university spokesperson said in a statement. “However, Ohio State elected not to participate in its game day activations in our home venues or on our sidelines or team bench areas while we are the visiting team.”

The spokesperson declined to elaborate on the school’s reasoning. But avoiding an association with the name “Strauss” seems an obvious consideration, given the sordid history of Richard Strauss, the school’s longtime former sports medicine doctor, whose decades of sexual abuse victimized hundreds of students and cost OSU more than $161 million in settlements.

It is unclear whether Ohio State communicated any concerns about the branding to the Big Ten or the company prior to the deal being announced. Spokespeople for both did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The school’s decision, first reported by WOSU Public Media, is a setback for the company now known simply as Strauss. The German manufacturer opened its U.S. headquarters—dubbed “The Fieldhouse”—in Columbus earlier this year, as well as a flagship retail store in the city this month. It also marks the second successive sports-related marketing complication for the privately held, family-owned manufacturer. As Sportico reported, Strauss has recently threatened to scale back its sponsorship role in the 2027 IIHF World Championship in Germany next year if the Russian national hockey team is permitted to participate.

Strauss upped its profile in the U.S. in 2024 with a sponsorship agreement that puts its logo on every batting helmet used during MLB’s postseason.

On Monday, the Big Ten named Strauss the conference’s “official workwear partner” as part of a multiyear, multisport sponsorship agreement. The deal will put the company’s branding across a range of Big Ten assets in the league’s football stadium and broadcasts, and it will feature a Strauss-branded red zone at the Big Ten Football Championship Game. The company will also receive sponsorship exposure during volleyball and basketball games.

In addition to pro baseball and hockey, Strauss—the German word for “ostrich”—has previously established partnerships across professional soccer, including the UEFA Europa League, Liverpool FC, Los Angeles FC and the Mexican national team. The Big Ten agreement is Strauss’ first foray into college athletics.

Ahead of its U.S. expansion, the company reportedly reached an agreement with Levi Strauss in 2019 allowing Engelbert Strauss to use the “Strauss” name on its clothing, including its popular workwear pants. The company’s CEO, Henning Strauss, previously attended Pepperdine University and has been a major donor to that school

To date, there are no known partnerships between Strauss and Ohio State, whose campus is just 2.4 miles away from “The Fieldhouse.”

In June, Ohio State’s board of trustees approved a $100 million settlement with 279 plaintiffs who alleged that they were sexually assaulted by Richard Strauss under the guise of his medical care. The university previously paid out $61 million to 317 other Strauss victims.

Strauss, who died by suicide in 2005, worked in the school’s athletic department from 1978 to 1996, and many of those he abused were former OSU athletes.

title: Formulate XP hires F1 sponsorship veteran Dan Staples as Founding Partner - Sector
article_text:
Formulate XP has appointed Dan Staples as Founding Partner and Managing Director.

Bringing nearly two decades of experience in sports sponsorship, he will shape the agency’s strategy and growth alongside Founder and Chief Executive Officer Ben McMahon.

The hire marks the senior-led sports marketing agency’s move from launch into delivery for the 2027 season, following the announcement of its five Driving Partners in October.

Staples will lead its client work and the senior team that owns the strategy, client relationships and delivery oversight for every programme.

He has worked on some of Formula 1’s biggest brand partnerships, including Santander’s programmes with Scuderia Ferrari and F1, and Petronas’ title partnership with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team.

Staples was also involved in Tata Communications’ F1 Innovation Prize, which crowdsourced ideas from fans and saw the winning one taken into incubation by F1, a world first for global sport.

“Too often, agencies are brought in downstream to activate an idea someone else has already had,” Staples said.

“The best agency partnerships start earlier than that, with the strategy and the creative thinking, and they’re held to account for what they deliver.

“Formulate XP is built to work that way: one senior team that owns the thinking from the start.

“That’s why I wanted to build it with Ben, and I can’t wait to get started with our clients and Driving Partners.”

Formulate XP delivers commercial and partnership strategy, data-led audience intelligence, PR and communications, corporate hospitality and events production, and content and amplification for brands and rightsholders.

“Dan has built some of the most distinctive brand partnerships in Formula 1, and he’s done it by thinking first and activating second,” McMahon said.

“That’s exactly the approach Formulate XP was founded on. Having Dan as a Founding Partner gives us the senior leadership to scale the agency and the work we do for our clients.”

title: Rugby Australia Re-Signs Qantas as Official Airline Partner in Three-Year Deal
article_text:
Rugby Australia has secured a commercial return, signing national carrier Qantas as its Official Airline Partner under a comprehensive three-year agreement.

The deal installs Qantas as Principal Partner of both the Australian Women’s and Men’s Sevens teams, placing the Qantas logo across the front of both playing jerseys, alongside Major Partner designations for the Wallabies and Wallaroos.

The agreement marks Qantas’ first major sponsorship return to Australian rugby since exiting its 30-year Wallabies partnership during the pandemic in 2020, aligning the carrier across all four senior national squads ahead of a major home international cycle culminating in the Men’s Rugby World Cup Australia 2027.

Rugby Australia CEO, Phil Waugh, welcomed the return of the national carrier as a significant commercial endorsement ahead of home major events.

“For three golden decades, the Qantas brand was synonymous with some of Australian Rugby’s greatest moments and we are delighted to welcome back Australia’s national airline at a truly defining time for the game in this country.”

“As the Official Airline of Rugby Australia, Principal Partner of the Australian Women’s and Men’s Sevens Teams and Major Partner of the Wallabies and Wallaroos, Qantas’ re-entry to Australian Rugby represents much more than the rekindling of an old friendship.

“It is also a launchpad into a bright future. Like Australian Rugby, Qantas has risen from humble beginnings to proudly represent our great nation on the global stage.

“To have The Spirit of Australia back behind all four of our Teams in Gold is a powerful statement and a source of immense pride for the entire rugby community,” Waugh said.

Qantas International CEO, Cam Wallace highlighted the commercial appeal of backing Australian national teams as global rugby prepares to centre on Australia.

“Qantas has always been proud to support Australian athletes and teams competing on the world stage.”

“It’s an incredible time for Australian rugby, with some of the sport’s biggest international events ahead, and we’re excited to be partnering with Rugby Australia as the world turns its attention to Australia,” Wallace said.

Launching immediately at the season-opening HSBC SVNS tournament in Dubai on 28–29 November 2026, the three-year term spans a high-visibility international calendar through late 2029.

With the Australian Women’s Sevens entering the 2026–27 campaign as reigning world champions, Qantas will also activate at the grassroots level by granting every registered junior rugby player in Western Australia from the 2026 and 2027 seasons complimentary entry to the HSBC Perth SVNS at HBF Park on 6–7 February 2027.

title: New documents reveal SEC’s role in preventing mandatory media-rights pooling in PCSA
article_text:
Awful Announcing previously documented how ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro was lobbying New York Yankees President Randy Levine, a leader of the president’s college sports committee and advocate for the Protect College Sports Act, to protect the network’s television deal with the SEC. New documents show the goal was mutual from the SEC’s side.

Emails obtained via public records requests detail how one of the conference’s main objectives with the bill was keeping its lucrative media deal with ESPN and staying out of the PCSA’s proposed media pool. They show the SEC telling senators it wouldn’t support the PCSA unless media rights pooling was optional and telling its members to turn down meetings with the bill’s primary advocacy backer, Saving College Sports, because of the group’s support for the provision.

On Aug. 4, SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey emailed every SEC president and athletic director about a call scheduled for later that day. Organized by SCS with Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO), the call would address the next steps for the PCSA. The SEC had announced its support for the bill just days earlier.

The invitations cited conference support for the legislation and suggested conference leaders or school representatives would participate, Sankey wrote. Several SEC officials had contacted him to ask about the group and its invitation.

Sankey said he wouldn’t participate. He cited SCS’s support for “centralized media-rights negotiations for college football, greater national coordination of football scheduling in support of those media-rights objectives, and a national approach to distributing revenues generated through those media rights,” as reasons to oppose the bill. Those goals were “inconsistent with longstanding SEC principles and policy positions,” Sankey wrote.

He also instructed SEC officials to decline SCS invitations even when they came through significant donors, governing board chairs, or board members. Attendance, “even solely for informational purposes,” could later be characterized as support for the group’s objectives.

“Regardless of the source, I recommend that these invitations be respectfully declined,” Sankey wrote.

Saving College Sports declined comment for this story. As of publication, the SEC has not responded to Awful Announcing’s request for comment.

Records obtained from multiple SEC universities include a June 12 document listing the conference’s “red provisions” for the PCSA under the heading “Must be fixed.”

“There should be no question that joining the covered entity is voluntary and that declining to join has no legal ramifications,” the document stated. It called for an explicit prohibition on state or federal lawsuits challenging a decision to stay out of the pool. The SEC also wanted to prevent participating conferences or the pool itself from using new agreements or other actions to compromise nonparticipants’ rights or pressure them to join.

The document sought to exclude all postseason tournaments and contests from pooling. It warned that the bill could otherwise “interfere with existing tournaments, such as the College Baseball or Softball World Series.”

In a cover memo dated the same day, Sankey instructed presidents and athletic directors to call both of their senators before the committee markup. He supplied a script asking senators to support the conference and their school “by withholding your support for the Protect College Sports Act until essential revisions are made to strengthen the legislation.”

SEC talking points obtained from Texas stated: “We do not believe media rights pooling is necessary to stabilize college athletics.” The document argued that pooling legislation should be considered separately. The talking points said the SEC did not oppose other conferences and universities opting in. Its concern was that the proposal “exposes the SEC to potential lawsuits, forcing the conference into the media pooling practice.”

By July 26, Senate Commerce Committee staff members were offering changes to address those concerns. Sankey circulated a summary of proposed revisions that afternoon, along with an email from Brad Grantz, the committee’s majority staff director. Grantz described the attachment as a summary of changes “to secure [the SEC and Big Ten’s] support.”

“This is a substantial package, and much of it reflects what you have specifically asked us to change,” Grantz wrote. The attachment paired requests with proposed provisions. Under “Keep Media Rights Voluntary,” it said the act would not permit federal or state lawsuits challenging an institution’s or conference’s decision to stay out.

Another entry addressed scheduling. Earlier versions of the PCSA contained a traditional rivalry provision that would have required Oklahoma to put Oklahoma State back on its schedule and Missouri to do the same with Kansas. The Senate response said those requirements would apply only to institutions that voluntarily joined the pool. Schools and conferences that stayed out would be exempt, regardless of whether a game was a traditional rivalry.

Sankey wrote that the summary “reflects progress.” Grantz subsequently sent a “best-and-final offer,” copying Levine. The package included the voluntary participation and scheduling protections the SEC had sought.

“Pencils are down,” Grantz wrote. He demanded individual responses by 10 a.m. July 30 stating whether recipients supported the bill and would actively work to secure its passage.

On July 31, Sankey forwarded another message to SEC presidents saying the committee had “moved substantially in the SEC’s direction.” It cited voluntary participation, scheduling authority for nonparticipants, and protection from litigation intended to force them to join.

“There is no legislative alternative that gets better for the SEC,” the message warned. Further revisions protected existing television agreements, including ESPN’s SEC deal, from being overridden by a pool. The bill also expressly stated that conferences and institutions could not be required to join.

title: Lucozade signs Lionesses star Alessia Russo
article_text:
Lucozade has signed England and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo to a long-term partnership, adding one of women’s football’s biggest names to its athlete roster and building on 20 years of support for the Lionesses.

Russo joins after a standout year. She became the highest-scoring English player in UEFA Women’s Champions League history, was named England Women’s Player of the Year, finished in the top ten of the 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or and was named in the FIFPRO Women’s World 11.

The deal was unveiled at ‘Her Game. Her Fuel.’, an event in Shoreditch where Russo was interviewed by Ian Wright in front of athletes, creators, fans and cultural voices.

Alessia Russo said, “Football has always been a massive part of my life. Growing up, my dad would take me to watch women’s games at Charlton, and I remember looking up to those players and dreaming of doing the same one day. To see how far the game has come is incredible. Women’s football is now about so much more than what happens on the pitch. It’s influencing fashion, culture and bringing communities together in ways I could never have imagined growing up. To be part of that journey, and now working with Lucozade, a brand that’s supported the Lionesses for so many years, is really special.”

Under the partnership, Russo will work closely with Lucozade Sport to understand her individual hydration and fuelling needs and to explore how a more personalised approach can support her preparation, performance and recovery. She will also feed into future product innovation across the range. The road to the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil is a major focus, with England still chasing qualification through the play-offs.

Lucozade has backed the Lionesses since 2006 and is part of Suntory Beverage & Food GB&I, whose brands also include Ribena and Orangina.

Matt Riches, Head of Partnerships at Suntory Beverage & Food GB&I, said, “Sport is changing, and so are the ways people connect with it. Alessia represents a new generation of athletes whose influence extends far beyond the pitch, inspiring more young women and girls to engage with sport in their own way.“

“She’s not only one of the most exciting talents in world football, but someone who is helping shape the culture around women’s sport, and we’re incredibly proud to welcome her to the Lucozade family.“

title: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
article_text:
The NFL has gotten a little bit cheesier this season—and fans can’t just blame the league’s scriptwriters.

Earlier this year, Kraft Heinz inked a five-year, global partnership with the league for brands in its portfolio including Kraft, Velveeta, Philadelphia, and Kraft Mac & Cheese. It’s the first time multiple Kraft Heinz brands have been involved in the same long-term partnership, according to Ryan Djabbarah, the company’s head of sports and entertainment marketing—and halfway through the season, his team is already seeing results.

Their strategy, Djabbarah told Marketing Brew, has been based largely on weaving Kraft Heinz brands into NFL fan experiences in ways that are whimsical and funny while also adding value—like their latest activation, which reimagines end-zone pylons as blocks of cheese for Thanksgiving weekend as part of a Velveeta product giveaway.

“We want to make sure that we’re thinking about our products in a way that engages fans…in ways that they didn’t expect before from our brands,” Djabbarah said. “It felt like we should have been doing this a long time ago, and now that we’re finally here, I’m hopeful you’ll see a lot more of these ideas…coming to the table.”

The activation, Djabbarah said, was an easy yes once the team spotted the opportunity.

“That’s been hiding in plain sight the whole time—these Velveeta blocks looking like a pylon,” he said. “It just was too obvious and too opportunistic for us not to lean into, and hopefully [we’ll] lean into it even longer-term after Thanksgiving as well.”

The pylons themselves won’t carry Velveeta branding, but in the modern sports marketing landscape, there’s hardly an asset that isn’t up for sale, and Djabbarah said Velveeta-branded pylons aren’t out of the realm of possibility.

“It’s not to say we won’t go after it…at a later date, but there’s so few brands that are able to affect the actual in-game…that we don’t have that aspiration just yet,” he told us.

It’s not the first time in the short history of Kraft Heinz’s partnership with the NFL that the company has touted its portfolio of cheese-centric brands, and it won’t be the last, Djabbarah said. Earlier this season, cheeseburger enthusiast and Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid teamed up with Kraft Singles for a giveaway campaign, and Djabbarah said the brand is cooking up another NFL campaign set to roll out next month.

Heinz Tomato Ketchup, long associated with football since its parent company’s name used to adorn Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, has also been an early fixture of the partnership. The brand now sponsors Prime Video’s “Red Zone Moments” highlights, and it also showed up in a big way around this year’s NFL Draft in Pittsburgh with “Mr. 57,” its new program honoring the 57th pick.

Stunts like these seem to be paying off: During the week of that activation in April, Heinz dollar sales increased by 20% compared to the same week in 2025, Djabbarah told us.

“To see that kind of success in just our first bite at the apple was a lot of fun,” he said.

While revenue growth is a main goal of the partnership, Djabbarah said he and his team are also looking to drive brand love and preference, especially during key periods for the company when the NFL plays, like back-to-school season and the holidays.

With the Super Bowl coming on the heels of the holiday season, Kraft Heinz marketers are already thinking about how to bring their brands to that game, too. For Djabbarah, that doesn’t necessarily mean a traditional TV ad buy; instead, Kraft Heinz brands are more likely to show up through customer hospitality programs and retail activations, similarly to how his team has leveraged the official NFL sponsorship thus far.

“In the past, we’ve had to say ‘Big Game,’ or never really talk about tickets,” he said. “Now, we have an opportunity not only to use the logo in an authentic way that we’re seeing success already from, but also [to] bring some fun personalities into it as well.”

title: NASCAR Sponsorship Fallout Grows as Federal Investigation Uncovers Shocking Allegations
article_text:
New details in federal court filings have raised fresh questions about the alleged misuse of investor money connected to Droplight and motorsports sponsorships. A Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) complaint alleges that Phillip Williams, co-founder of Droplight, used more than $11 million in investor funds for an “apparent auto racing team.”

The filing does not identify the team. Motorsports reporter Bob Pockrass of FOX Sports also highlighted an alleged $500,000 payment for an “apparent auto racing sponsorship” linked to Williams’ associate Devin Johnson. The allegations form part of a wider investigation into Backward Hat Capital, which authorities claim raised more than $550 million from investors through a Ponzi-style scheme. Williams and Johnson were arrested on November 18.

The CFTC complaint alleges that more than $11 million in investor funds went toward an apparent auto racing team. It also claims Devin Johnson spent $500,000 from the same pool of money on an apparent racing sponsorship. However, investigators have not named the teams involved in either transaction.

The alleged motorsports spending forms part of a wider list of transfers that authorities say involved investor money. The complaint also lists more than $3.2 million in apparent real estate purchases, $3 million paid to an apparent bare-knuckle fighting promoter, and more than $1.8 million for luxury car garage space.

The CFTC alleges that these payments involved money belonging to participants in the Backward Hat Capital enterprise. The allegations remain unproven and have not been tested at trial.

Federal authorities allege that Backward Hat Capital raised more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants beginning around July 2022. The enterprise allegedly promised monthly returns exceeding 6% with no losing months through leveraged foreign-exchange trading.

However, prosecutors claim little to no actual forex trading took place. Instead, the alleged scheme used money from new investors to pay earlier participants, while large sums went to the people behind the operation.

The criminal complaint alleges that more than $200 million went toward investor redemptions. Authorities also claim accounts controlled by Williams received more than $130 million, while accounts connected to Johnson received over $40 million.

Williams and Johnson were arrested on November 18. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York charged them with securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and conspiracy to commit securities fraud.

Droplight built a presence in motorsports during 2025, sponsoring Louis Foster’s No. 45 Honda at Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing, including the Indianapolis 500. RLL later announced a long-term extension with the company.

The brand also appeared in the NASCAR Truck Series and other racing categories through related sponsorships. Johnson’s company SalesAi separately sponsored Dreyer & Reinbold Racing’s No. 24 entry in recent Indianapolis 500 events, although that connection does not appear in the regulatory allegations.

The SEC has filed a separate civil lawsuit and secured a court-ordered freeze on assets. Its complaint identifies Droplight LLC as a relief defendant and alleges the company received $31 million originating from Backward Hat investors through KMAP Inc.

Following the arrests, Droplight disappeared from RLL’s listed partners, and its websites went offline. Racing teams are reviewing their agreements as the cases move forward. The court filings have not identified the teams connected to the alleged $11 million and $500,000 racing expenditures, leaving those sponsorship details unresolved.

title: Sydney Thunder and Cricket Victoria Announce Sponsorship Deals with Bargain Car Rentals and ISLA Vodka for 2026/27 Season
article_text:
Sydney Thunder has named Bargain Car Rentals as its Official Car Rental Partner for both Weber WBBL|12 and KFC BBL|16, while Cricket Victoria has renewed its partnership with Victorian vodka brand ISLA Vodka for the 2026/27 season.

The agreement between Sydney Thunder and Bargain Car Rentals covers both the men’s and women’s competitions simultaneously, with the Bargain Car Rentals logo to feature on the front left of Thunder’s playing pants across both WBBL and BBL squads.

Bargain Car Rentals was founded in Hobart more than 20 years ago and now serves more than 250,000 customers per year across 14 locations nationwide. The company is scheduled to open a new Canberra depot in March 2027, expanding its footprint in Sydney Thunder’s second home territory.

Sydney Thunder’s BBL|16 campaign opens in Canberra on December 16, 2026, before the team returns to ENGIE Stadium for the Sydney Smash on December 19, 2026.

Cricket Victoria has extended its partnership with ISLA Vodka into the 2026/27 season following an initial arrangement that ran through 2025/26. ISLA Vodka is a Victorian-owned and distilled brand producing vodka and ready-to-drink beverages.

Under the renewed agreement, ISLA Vodka will be available at selected Cricket Victoria functions, events, and hospitality activations throughout the season at Junction Oval.

Both announcements reflect a pattern of franchises and state associations securing partnerships that span men’s and women’s cricket properties within a single commercial arrangement. The Bargain Car Rentals deal with Sydney Thunder covers Weber WBBL|12 and KFC BBL|16 concurrently, committing the brand to visibility across both competitions from the outset of the season.

The partnership announcements were made in November 2026, ahead of the start of the BBL and WBBL competitive seasons.

title: Major League Fishing Announces Multi-Year Sponsorship Renewal with Tackle Warehouse
article_text:
BENTON, Ky. (Nov. 24, 2026) – Major League Fishing (MLF) announced today a multiyear sponsorship renewal with Tackle Warehouse, a leading online retailer of fishing tackle and equipment. The three-year agreement extends the companies’ longstanding partnership, with Tackle Warehouse continuing as the title sponsor of the Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit and an Official Tackle Retailer of MLF5.

A valued MLF partner since 2020, Tackle Warehouse has played an integral role in supporting competitive bass fishing across multiple levels of the sport. The renewed agreement reinforces the retailer’s commitment to tournament anglers while maintaining its prominent presence throughout MLF’s professional and grassroots tournament platforms.

The 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit will showcase top professional anglers competing across six premier fisheries for the sport’s biggest payouts outside of the Bass Pro Tour, valuable points toward Pro Circuit Championship qualification and opportunities to advance to REDCREST and the Bass Pro Tour.

“Tournament fishing has always been an important part of who we are at Tackle Warehouse, and our partnership with Major League Fishing allows us to stay closely connected to the action and help drive this sport forward,” said Joey Reggio, General Manager at Tackle Warehouse. “We’re proud to back a circuit that gives anglers a real shot at their dreams and gives fans a front-row seat to some of the best tournament bass fishing anywhere.  We’re anglers ourselves, and we’re excited to keep supporting the sport we love.”

Tackle Warehouse will maintain brand visibility across all MLF5 media platforms, including television airings on VICE TV and MLFNOW! livestream coverage on MajorLeagueFishing.com, the MyOutdoorTV (MOTV) app and Rumble, providing opportunities to showcase Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories to the tournament fishing community.

“Tackle Warehouse has been a tremendous partner to Major League Fishing and a trusted resource for our anglers, whether they’re gearing up for their first BFL or preparing for a Pro Circuit event,” said Jake Wittkop, MLF Vice President and Managing Director of Sponsorship and Business Development. “Their continued investment in the Pro Circuit and MLF5 helps give anglers the opportunity to compete close to home and work their way up to the national stage. We’re proud to build on this partnership over the next three years.”

The Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit kicks off Feb. 18-20 at Lake Murray in Columbia, South Carolina, before traveling to Chickamauga Lake in Tennessee, Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Texas, Clarks Hill Lake in Georgia, the Arkansas River in Oklahoma and the St. Lawrence River in New York. The season will culminate Sept. 10-12 at the Pro Circuit Championship on the James River in Richmond, Virginia.

Anglers who aspire to fish the 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit may enter by calling Major League Fishing at 270.252.1000.

For more information about MLF, its tournaments and sponsors, visit MajorLeagueFishing.com. To explore Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories, visit TackleWarehouse.com .

Tackle Warehouse is the premier online shop for all of your bass angling needs. They provide the industry’s best gear, customer service, in-depth knowledge of products, tips and techniques from pros, as well as fast, efficient shipping. For more information visit TackleWarehouse.com   and follow them on social media at Facebook, X,  YouTube  and Instagram.

title: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 Highlights the Role of Digital Connectivity in International Travel
article_text:
Heading to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026? Enjoy every moment beyond the racetrack with Simigo. Stay connected while navigating Abu Dhabi, sharing race-day highlights, and exploring the city during your F1 trip.

As international fans prepare for the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026, Simigo highlights how travel eSIMs can support mobile connectivity abroad.

The Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 is scheduled for December 3–6 at Yas Marina Circuit, bringing together international motorsport fans for a weekend of racing and entertainment. The event also offers visitors opportunities to explore Abu Dhabi’s attractions and experiences beyond the circuit.

Attending a major international sporting event often involves more than watching the race. title: From Naming Rights to Brand Ownership: ENGIE Open 2026 Connecting Tennis, Local Culture, and Immersion in the Sport
article_text:
Florianópolis, November 2026 – Recognized for its ongoing investment in the development of tennis in Brazil, ENGIE Brasil reinforces the role of sport as a strategic pillar for relationship-building and brand development. At the ENGIE Open 2026—taking place from November 22 to 29 at the Lagoa Iate Clube (LIC)—the company, in collaboration with the agency Paim, is bringing a comprehensive experience to the courts of the Santa Catarina capital. This approach marks an evolution in the brand’s presence at the event, integrating a unique visual identity—inspired by local traditions—with an experiential framework designed to engage everyone from the general public to business and institutional leaders.

The strategy developed for this edition is built upon an experiential framework featuring three levels of engagement, tailored to different audience profiles: the “Open” level (aimed at the general public and fans, offering free arena access, high-performance matches, a social hub, and the official event store); the “Experience” level (featuring active, scheduled activities such as sports clinics, on-court challenges, and exclusive interactions with athletes); and the “Exclusive” level (a platform for hospitality and strategic networking).

“The ENGIE Open reflects the continuous maturation of our support for tennis in Brazil—a commitment that goes far beyond mere visual association with the sport. With each edition, we enhance what we deliver, ensuring the tournament functions as a true engagement platform. By bringing together elite-level sport, gender equity, clean energy, and local development, we are able to translate ENGIE’s purpose into tangible, memorable touchpoints with the city, our clients, and the community,” states Michele Schifino, Director of Communication and Marketing at ENGIE Brasil.

To engage authentically with the capital of Santa Catarina, Paim developed a unique visual identity system for the event. It features textures, colors, and graphic elements inspired by five icons of the island: the blossoms of the Garapuvu (the city’s symbolic tree), the contours of the dunes at Lagoa da Conceição, the undulation of the sea, the geometry of fishermen’s nets, and the centuries-old patterns of traditional bobbin lace.

This cultural connection finds its ultimate physical expression in the tournament trophy: collector’s-edition racquets featuring hand-woven bobbin lace “strings.” These were crafted by artisans supported by the “Mulheres do Nosso Bairro” (“Women of Our Neighborhood”) social project, an initiative maintained by ENGIE. The production process, as carried out by the lace-makers, was documented in an audiovisual series.

“We worked to ensure the ENGIE Open possessed an identity that functioned like a major, independent event brand, while simultaneously breathing the spirit of ‘Floripa’ in every detail. From the color palette to the trophy itself, every element was designed to celebrate local culture and create a lasting aesthetic impression,” notes Samir Arrage, Creative Director at Paim.

The event’s product strategy adopted a branding-oriented approach: the ENGIE Open Store was structured around the concept that merchandising should serve as an extension of the brand into people’s daily lives. The collection features essential sports items and lifestyle products—such as polo shirts, scarves with exclusive prints, canvas and eco-leather tote bags, microfiber towels, and thermal bottles. All profits from sales will be donated to the Fundação Tênis (Tennis Foundation), an organization that supports the civic development of approximately 100 young people from communities in Florianópolis through sport.

The brand’s engagement journey extends beyond the club. At Florianópolis International Airport (Floripa Airport), arriving passengers and the roughly 130 participating athletes are welcomed by a scenic activation featuring an immersive court and a ball machine. This setup incorporates a cross-selling mechanism, offering prizes that can be collected at the tournament arena.

At the LIC sports complex, the ENGIE stand integrates interactive stations utilizing technology and gamification. These include “Target Serve” challenges, an electronic “Tennis Reflex” activity, a brand quiz, and clean-energy charging kiosks. Furthermore, the event incorporates sustainability management in partnership with the startup Descarbonize, which is responsible for a comprehensive greenhouse gas emissions inventory for environmental offsetting. The initiative also includes waste sorting protocols and the full repurposing of all scenic structures.

title: e.l.f. NWSL Sponsorship Grows Youth Reach as Glow For Glory Draws 1,200 Entries
article_text:
- e.l.f.’s Glow For Glory contest drew more than 1,200 submissions from U.S. girls ages 13 to 18 in 2026, the company said.

- A new partnership with Rush Soccer, a network of more than 25,000 girls and women players, scaled the contest this year.

- Five finalists were selected to carry the official Championship Match Ball roughly 250 miles from New York to Washington, D.C.

- e.l.f. became the NWSL’s first-ever beauty sponsor in March 2025 and presents the NWSL Challenge Cup through 2027.

The business of youth sports, first in your search results.

e.l.f. Cosmetics and e.l.f. SKIN, brands of e.l.f. Beauty (NYSE: ELF), returned to the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) Championship for a second year and expanded the youth side of the e.l.f. NWSL sponsorship through its Glow For Glory contest. The contest received more than 1,200 submissions from girls ages 13 to 18 across the U.S. in 2026, according to a Nov. 17 company release, after e.l.f. partnered with Rush Soccer’s network of more than 25,000 girls and women players.

The 2026 NWSL Championship, presented by Google Pixel, was scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, live on CBS Television Network and Paramount+.

Glow For Glory invites submissions from youth female soccer players ages 13 to 18. From the 2026 pool, e.l.f. selected five finalists to travel to the championship, where one would be crowned the 2026 Glow For Glory winner, the company said.

The finalists were set to collect the official Championship Match Ball and carry it approximately 250 miles from New York to Washington, D.C. Pit stops included a meeting with an NWSL player from e.l.f.’s roster and an e.l.f. shopping spree at CVS Pharmacy, an Official Health & Wellness Partner of the NWSL.

On match day, the finalists were slated to join the March to the Match, presented by e.l.f., led by the Washington Commanders’ 50-member marching band and drumline in e.l.f. gear. e.l.f. said its Fan Fest activities would stream on the brand’s Twitch channel.

e.l.f. describes Glow For Glory as the grassroots layer of its NWSL partnership, built to create pathways for young girls to stay in the sport rather than only sponsoring the professional level.

Where the e.l.f. NWSL Sponsorship Fits in the Brand’s Women’s Sports Strategy

e.l.f. became the league’s first-ever beauty sponsor in March 2025 and serves as Presenting Partner of the NWSL Challenge Cup through 2027, per the release. The company said it identified women’s sports as a “beauty desert,” a space where no one was showing up, five years ago.

The brand’s NWSL player roster includes Ally Sentnor (Angel City FC), Jaedyn Shaw (Gotham FC), Jess Carter (Gotham FC) and Lo’eau LaBonta (Kansas City Current), with LaBonta listed in the release as competing in this year’s championship. Outside soccer, e.l.f. works with Billie Jean King, Katherine Legge, Flau’jae Johnson and Kendall Coyne, and has partnerships with the PWHL and Wonder Women Wrestling.

The sponsorship also carries a sales component. All season, e.l.f. ran what it calls a connected commerce ecosystem across Amazon, TikTok Live and social platforms, including Glow Up!, its Roblox makeup experience, which the company said converted NWSL moments into real-time sales.

“Year one proved we belonged in the game, year two proves we can change the game,” said Patrick O’Keefe, Chief Integrated Marketing Officer at e.l.f. Brands.

What Does e.l.f.’s Research Say About Girls Who Play?

A report produced with Parity, which the release calls the largest and broadest study of its kind, looked at “Everyday Athletes,” defined as women who played sports for at least three years before the end of high school or secondary school and now work, or recently worked, full time.

According to the report, Everyday Athletes are nearly 50% more likely to hold leadership roles at work than women who played less or no sports. They are 37% more likely to aspire to senior leadership and nearly 25% more likely to have negotiated their salary. Among Everyday Athletes with at least five years of work experience, 69% said the lessons they learned in sports are more important than ever in today’s workplace.

From 1,200 Entries to a Match Ball in D.C.

The contest’s growth comes as the league’s crowds rise. Through the first half of the 2026 season, the NWSL reported a 10% year-over-year increase in average fans per match and was on pace for a fourth consecutive season averaging more than 10,000 fans per match, according to the release.

For e.l.f., the Rush Soccer partnership gave Glow For Glory access to a youth network of more than 25,000 players this year. The brand’s Challenge Cup presenting deal runs through 2027, and the release did not say whether Glow For Glory will widen its age range or add new club partners next season.

title: Grand Park Naming Rights: Droplight Name Leaves Website After Co-Founder's Ponzi Charges
article_text:
- Droplight no longer appears on the Grand Park Sports Campus website, Current reported, about a year after its Nov. 12, 2025 naming rights announcement.

- Federal prosecutors allege Droplight co-founder Phillip Patrick Williams received more than $130 million from a $600 million Ponzi scheme run through Backward Hat Capital.

- The City of Westfield says no taxpayer money went into the deal, and operator GPSE controls naming rights under a 30-year agreement.

- Two people familiar with Droplight told the Indianapolis Business Journal the company spends more than $8 million a year on Indiana teams and properties.

The business of youth sports, first in your search results.

The Droplight name has come off Grand Park naming rights branding, at least online. Days after federal prosecutors unsealed fraud charges against Droplight co-founder Phillip Patrick Williams, “Droplight” no longer appears on the website of the 400-acre youth sports campus in Westfield, Indiana, Current Publishing reported on Nov. 24. Since late 2025, the facility had been branded the Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus.

Neither Grand Park’s operator nor the city has publicly announced an end to the agreement, whose terms were never disclosed, according to Current.

On Nov. 18, prosecutors in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed a complaint against Williams, 51, of Kokomo, Indiana, and Devin Allen Johnson, 29, of Zionsville, the co-founders of investment firm Backward Hat Capital, according to reporting by Shawn Henry. Each faces one count of securities fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit securities fraud.

The complaint alleges Backward Hat took in more than $600 million from more than 2,000 investors by marketing a foreign-exchange arbitrage strategy. According to the filing, more than $200 million from new investors paid off earlier ones, more than $130 million went to Williams and more than $40 million went to Johnson. The complaint does not mention Droplight. Both men are presumed innocent.

Droplight was formed in December 2024, and its Indiana Secretary of State filing lists Williams as manager and registered agent, The Indiana Lawyer and the Indianapolis Business Journal (IBJ) reported. Westfield’s 2025 naming rights release identified Williams as Droplight’s co-founder and owner. The company’s chief executive is Joseph Anderson.

Grand Park Sports and Entertainment (GPSE), not the City of Westfield, according to the city. Under a 30-year public-private partnership signed in December 2024, GPSE, a joint venture of Indy Sports and Entertainment and Westfield-based Bullpen Ventures LLC, operates the city-owned campus and has the right to grant naming and sponsorship rights and keep the revenue, Current reported.

City spokesperson Kayla Arnold told Current that Westfield set some limits on permissible sponsors, such as a restriction on tobacco-related businesses, but that selecting and negotiating those deals is solely GPSE’s responsibility. She said “the city has not committed taxpayer funds to the Droplight sponsorship” and that it has no contractual payment obligations to Droplight.

GPSE pays the city a set operating fee that is expected to total $184 million over 30 years, starting at about $2.67 million in 2025 and rising to about $5 million a year by the end of the initial 10-year term, according to Current.

GPSE Vice President of Marketing and Communication Brad Hauter did not address the naming rights deal in a statement to Current. He said the company is aware of the allegations involving individuals associated with Droplight and will continue to monitor the situation.

Grand Park was one piece of a broader spend. Two people familiar with Droplight’s business told IBJ the company pays Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing at least $5 million to be lead sponsor of Louis Foster’s No. 45 IndyCar, and that its annual spending on Indiana teams and properties tops $8 million, including roughly $1 million a year to Butler University athletics. Butler said it is reviewing its agreement.

If a court-appointed receiver or bankruptcy trustee later traces Droplight’s payments back to Backward Hat investors, the properties that received them could face clawback claims. Under Section 548(c) of the Bankruptcy Code, a recipient can keep money to the extent it gave value and took the payment in good faith.

The closest precedent involves the Golf Channel, which kept about $5.9 million in advertising payments from R. Allen Stanford’s Ponzi scheme after the Texas Supreme Court ruled in 2016 that market-rate advertising sold in an arm’s-length deal had value when delivered, Henry reported. That ruling applied Texas law and does not bind other courts.

As of Nov. 20, Henry reported finding no public receivership or bankruptcy filing for Backward Hat or Droplight. Until a fiduciary is appointed to trace the money, it remains unknown whether any dollars behind the Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus name came from Backward Hat investors.

title: Weightlifting and Wrestling Sign Sponsorship Deals Worth Up to 1.4 Billion Won Over Three Years with IBK
article_text:
The Korean Weightlifting Federation and the Korea Wrestling Federation have signed official sponsorship agreements with IBK Industrial Bank of Korea.

Yesterday, on November 24, the two federations signed agreements at the IBK headquarters in Euljiro, Seoul, securing up to 1.4 billion won in financial support over the next three years.

This agreement continues the sponsorship that began with their initial partnership in 2022. The funds will be used for domestic and overseas training camps for national team athletes ahead of major international events including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, as well as for improving training environments, fostering promising young athletes, and promoting grassroots sports.

Choi Sung-yong, president of the Korean Weightlifting Federation, expressed gratitude for the bank's continued support, stating that they will do their utmost to help athletes make a greater leap forward and achieve valuable results ahead of the LA Olympics.

Chang Min-young, president of IBK, stated that the bank will lend its support so that athletes can fully showcase their skills and future prospects can nurture their dreams.

title: Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images Launch Inclusive Community Sport Visual Library
article_text:
The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) has partnered with global visual content creator Getty Images to launch a dedicated visual library designed to modernise how grassroots sport is represented across Australia.

The collection is delivered under Play Well, Australia’s first national sport participation strategy, co-designed with the sector in 2023, and debuts with 250 authentic still images and videos spanning athletics, equestrian, netball, badminton, and football. By resolving a long-standing marketing bottleneck for national sporting organisations (NSOs) and local clubs, the initiative supplies sector-wide communications teams with representative promotional assets ahead of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

ASC executive general manager of sport system impact and chair of the Play Well Leadership Group, Richard McInnes, highlighted the commercial and participation impact of equipping sports with authentic visual storytelling tools.

“Play Well is built on the belief that everyone has a place in sport.”

“We know the way sport is represented can influence whether people feel welcome and believe there is a place for them.

“This partnership will give sporting organisations access to authentic images, to use in promotional material and communication, that actually reflects the diversity of the people, communities and experiences that make Australian sport so special.

“It is another practical step towards breaking down barriers to participation and ensuring more people can see themselves being involved in sport,” McInnes said.

Getty Images senior director of custom and creative partnerships, Svetlana Zhukova, emphasised the role of representative media in reshaping community perceptions ahead of Brisbane 2032.

“Sport has an extraordinary ability to connect people, but the images used to represent it don’t always reflect who is actually taking part.”

“Through the partnership, we’re giving sports organisations, media and communities access to imagery that better reflects the diversity of Australian sport as the country looks towards Brisbane 2032,” Zhukova said.

Produced in collaboration with community clubs and inclusion bodies—including Sport Inclusion Australia, Metropolitan Districts Netball Association, Footscray Rangers Football Club, and Melbourne Smashers Badminton, the library reflects diverse ages, cultural backgrounds, genders, and physical abilities. Sporting bodies and sector partners can request direct access to the asset bank via the ASC marketing team, with additional sports scheduled for production and integration throughout 2027.

title: Buggyra and JJ Sport launch strategic long-term partnership as Aliyyah Koloc becomes factory driver
article_text:
-- Buggyra ZM Racing and Chinese racing team JJ Sport have announced a strategic long-term partnership covering joint racing activities, race car development, global logistics and international business operations. The agreement strengthens Buggyra's presence in China and gives JJ Sport access to Buggyra's operations in the Middle East and Central Europe. As part of the partnership, Buggyra driver Aliyyah Koloc will become a factory driver for JJ Sport from the 2027 season, racing the JJ3 car in T1+, the top category of rally-raid racing, with full technical support. The partnership was announced at a press conference in Prague today.

The agreement builds on a collaboration that has grown over the past two years. Buggyra took part in the Taklimakan Rally, one of the world's longest and most difficult cross-country rallies, in 2025 and 2026, with Aliyyah finishing tenth overall this year. In 2026, the team also competed in a JJ Sport-supported operation for the first time, as a guest entry. Aliyyah has also contested several rounds of the China Cross-Country Rally Series (CCR) this year with support from JJ Sport.

JJ Sport is the racing arm of Hebei-based Jiujiang Group. It built China's first FIA-homologated rally car and now fields the JJ3 T1+ mainly in Chinese events. Both organizations will remain independent while cooperating beyond racing.

Buggyra Performance, the team's technical arm, will become JJ Sport's strategic partner for international operations. It will be responsible for global logistics, spare parts distribution, sales of JJ Sport race cars and operational support in the Middle East, Central Europe and other international markets.

Martin Koloc, Aliyyah's father and team principal of Buggyra ZM Racing, said: "I believe this is a major milestone in the history of both our teams and the Buggyra brand. For the first time, we have the opportunity to join a factory team with full support and highest-priority access to all technical developments, upgrades, and spare parts. Today, in Europe and around the world, we are seeing increasingly long lead times and difficulties supplying spare parts. Having priority access is therefore a significant advantage for us.

"Our partnership is not limited to racing and race team operations. We have also agreed to cooperate on technical development. We are already involved in developing the car for 2028, contributing a great deal of our own expertise and technology. I believe this will be a significant step forward for both JJ Sport and Buggyra in terms of competitiveness against traditional automotive manufacturers. Buggyra will also become the commercial representative for JJ Sport products in the Middle East and Central Europe."

From the 2027 season, Aliyyah will race for JJ Sport as a factory driver in a JJ3 car built and serviced by JJ Sport for the main events of her season. She will be the only non-Chinese and only female driver in the team's factory line-up.

At 22, Aliyyah has raced trucks, EuroNASCAR, GT4 and GT3 cars, and rally raids. She won the FIA Middle East Baja T3 Cup in her rookie season in 2022 and the 24 Hour GT4 Series title in 2024. In 2023, she became the youngest woman to start the Dakar Rally, at 18, in the T3 category.

"We have been following Aliyyah for many years. She is a very strong driver with excellent driving skills and, of course, she has benefited from Martin's guidance and training," said Xiaogang Deng, team principal of JJ Sport. "At JJ Sport, we are truly honored to welcome her to our team, which will field seven race cars next season. We also see this as a great opportunity to establish ourselves on the global motorsport stage.

"The Chinese automotive industry is currently developing at a remarkable pace, and the same applies to motorsport. Of course, we have not yet reached the level of our American or European counterparts, but I believe this gap will gradually narrow. We are therefore very excited about the future. I also believe that through our partnership with Buggyra, we will develop increasingly competitive race cars and continue to grow stronger together."

Aliyyah added: "I'm very happy to be named a JJ Sport factory driver and to be racing with the team. It's a great opportunity, and the support is amazing, from technical expertise to translations and logistics. It makes a real difference to have a team that can offer so much help in a country we don't know very well ourselves yet."

The joint 2027 program, with Aliyyah as the driver for both teams, will include the FIA Middle East Baja Championship, the Taklimakan Rally and the CCR. The first race is scheduled to be the Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge in March 2027. Aliyyah will continue to race with Buggyra alongside her JJ Sport program, with further details to be confirmed early next year.

Aliyyah will not compete in the T1+ category at the Dakar Rally in January 2027. She will instead serve as a test and reserve driver for Buggyra's truck team at the rally. Martin explained the decision: "We will not be taking part in the 2027 Dakar Rally in the T1+ category. Our car does not meet the required technical specifications, our entire infrastructure is based in the Middle East, and the location of the Dakar has changed. We have therefore decided to focus on the development of the car, the 2027 racing season and preparations for the 2028 Dakar Rally."

Both teams are now preparing a joint operation at the 2028 Dakar Rally. Buggyra will announce further Dakar plans for its truck team at a press conference on December 8.
